title: U.S. House · Michigan's 1st District
area: Michigan's 1st Congressional District — the Upper Peninsula and the northern Lower Peninsula (Traverse City, Marquette, Sault Ste. Marie).

context.text: Cook Political Report rated Michigan's 1st District R+11 for the 2026 cycle. Donald Trump won the district 59.9%–38.7% in 2024.

Incumbent Jack Bergman defeated Matthew DenOtter and Justin Michal in the August 4, 2026 Republican primary with 74.7% of the vote. Callie Barr defeated Kyle Blomquist and Wayne Stiles in the Democratic primary with 56.3% of the vote.

candidates.name: Jack Bergman
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary with 74.7% of the vote

summary.text: Bergman is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Michigan's 1st District, first elected in 2016. He retired from the U.S. Marine Corps as a lieutenant general after a 40-year military career, worked as a commercial airline pilot and small-business owner, and sits on the House Armed Services, Veterans' Affairs and Budget committees. He is seeking re-election after winning the August 4, 2026 Republican primary.

background.text: Born in Shakopee, Minnesota, in 1947. His official biography says he grew up in the Midwest and that his family's Michigan roots go back to ancestors who worked as iron miners in the Upper Peninsula in the late 1800s.
Earned a bachelor's degree in business from Gustavus Adolphus College (1969) and an MBA from the University of Western Florida.
Served in the U.S. Marine Corps from 1969 to 2009, retiring as a lieutenant general; his official biography describes 40 years in uniform.

Worked as a commercial airline pilot for 22 years and, according to his official biography, launched two startup businesses in the medical equipment field while in the military and owned and operated a small business.
According to his official biography, he and his wife, Cindy, settled in Watersmeet, on the western edge of the Upper Peninsula, nearly three decades ago; he has ten grandchildren.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2016 and first took office in 2017. His official biography describes him as the highest-ranking combat veteran ever to serve in the House.

Committee assignments for 2025-2026: House Armed Services (chair of the Readiness subcommittee), House Veterans' Affairs and House Budget. Earlier terms included Natural Resources (2017-2018) and chairing the Armed Services Intelligence and Special Operations subcommittee (2023-2024).
Won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary with 74.7% of the vote over Matthew DenOtter and Justin Michal.

priorities.text: Says he has used his role on the House Veterans' Affairs Committee to work on toxic exposure, mental health, and expanding Veterans' access to community care.

Highlights his work supporting Michigan's agriculture industry, including advocacy for the USMCA trade agreement and against unfair foreign trade practices affecting Michigan cherry, apple, dairy, and other growers.
Points to his role securing Great Lakes Restoration Initiative funding and combating invasive species such as Asian carp as a priority for protecting the region's natural resources.

positions.summary: Campaign issues page says he supported the Secure the Border Act, the Laken Riley Act's expanded detention requirements and the One Big Beautiful Bill Act's increased funding for border and immigration enforcement.
positions.quote: He also supported the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which provided major new investments in border security and immigration enforcement, including resources for border infrastructure, personnel, detention capacity, and efforts to stop fentanyl trafficking.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025–2026), serves on the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs (Disability Assistance and Memorial Affairs; Health) and the House Committee on Armed Services, chairing the Readiness Subcommittee, and on the House Committee on the Budget.

candidates.name: Callie Barr
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary with 56.3% of the vote

summary.text: Barr is an attorney and former high school English teacher from Traverse City and the Democratic nominee for Michigan's 1st District. She was the party's nominee against Rep. Jack Bergman in 2024 and won the 2026 primary to face him again.

background.text: Born and raised in Traverse City, moving to Cheboygan in high school, according to a 2024 Northern Express profile.
Earned a degree in secondary education from Central Michigan University and later a law degree from the University of Michigan, according to Northern Express.

Worked as a high school English teacher in several schools as her family moved; Northern Express reports her husband enlisted in the U.S. Marine Corps after September 11, 2001, and that she became involved in advocacy for military families through Blue Star Families and the Rosalynn Carter Institute for Caregivers.
Works as an attorney; local TV coverage describes her as an attorney, military spouse and teacher.
Was the Democratic nominee in 2024, receiving 37.9% (180,937 votes) to Bergman's 59.2% in the general election.
Announced in July 2025 that she would run again, saying she would focus on health care, veterans and rural communities.
Won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary over Kyle Blomquist and Wayne Stiles.

priorities.text: Making housing, income, food and health care more affordable.
priorities.quote: Callie Barr is focused on the basics families talk about around the kitchen table: a home they can afford, work that pays, food on the table, and care close to home.

positions.summary: Campaign website lists protecting Medicaid and rural hospitals from cuts, extending ACA subsidies and supporting a strong public option.
positions.quote: Extend ACA subsidies and support a strong public option.

positions.summary: Campaign website calls for ending tariffs that hurt farmers and raise food prices.
positions.quote: End tariffs that hurt farmers and raise food prices.

positions.summary: Campaign platform lists zoning reform among her housing proposals.
positions.quote: Support practical zoning reform so homes actually get built.

positions.summary: Her 2024 campaign website supports background checks, safe storage and red flag laws.
positions.quote: she supports common sense solutions that are supported by a majority of Americans and Michiganders, including background checks, safe storage, and red flag laws to prevent firearm related injuries, school shootings, and domestic violence

candidates.researchNotes: Positions come from her 2026 campaign platform page, her campaign website text archived by Ballotpedia in July 2024 (guns, police funding), and an Oct. 2026 WCMU interview. Her statement on women's health care in the 2024 text did not name abortion, so no abortion position was recorded.

statements.context: On her campaign platform page (undated; accessed Oct. 19, 2026)

statements.context: On her campaign website as archived by Ballotpedia (accessed July 24, 2024)

statements.quote: But what you can do is help to advance towards a clean energy future.

candidates.name: LaVeta Davenport

summary.text: Davenport is the Green Party nominee for Michigan's 1st District, advancing from the Green Party convention on July 18, 2026. According to Ballotpedia, she is the founder of a nonprofit organization.

background.text: Ballotpedia lists her as the founder of Levadeh, a nonprofit organization that focuses on health, education, relationship and ownership.

priorities.text: Making everyday costs such as groceries and gas affordable.
priorities.quote: And this is things like putting groceries on the table. That should be affordable.

priorities.text: A universal basic income of $1,000 per month, which she describes as a Green Party goal.
priorities.quote: the vision and goal of the Green Party includes something called the universal basic income

positions.summary: Said in an Oct. 2026 WCMU interview that she is opposed to the current administration's tariffs.
positions.quote: I do not agree with the way the current administration initiated the tariffs or the reasoning for placing them, and so that is something that I am thoroughly opposed to.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and priorities come from an Oct. 13, 2026 WCMU/Civic Media interview. No campaign website, Ballotpedia survey or other questionnaire found; her answers on Iran, data centers and Line 5 do not squarely match guide issues.

candidates.name: Arnett Satterla

summary.text: Satterla is the Libertarian Party nominee for Michigan's 1st District, advancing from the Libertarian convention on June 28, 2026.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, Ballotpedia survey, news interview or voter-guide answers found as of Oct. 19, 2026 (checked Ballotpedia, Planet Detroit and Michigan Advance voter guides, web searches).

candidates.name: Doc Kovaly

summary.text: Kovaly is the U.S. Taxpayers Party nominee for Michigan's 1st District, advancing from the party's convention on July 18, 2026.

priorities.quote: Until they can speak, we will speak for them.

positions.summary: Campaign website is centered on ending abortion.
positions.quote: To end abortion, we too must show the victims.

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign website (doc.vote) is a single-issue page on abortion with fundraising appeals; it lists no positions on other guide issues. No Ballotpedia survey or questionnaire found.

candidates.name: Liz Hakola

summary.text: Hakola is the Working Class Party nominee for Michigan's 1st District, advancing from the party's convention on June 6, 2026. She appeared on the district's general-election ballot in 2022 and 2024.

background.text: Ballotpedia lists her as a general-election candidate for Michigan's 1st District in 2022 and 2024; in 2024 she ran on the Working Class Party line and received 1.8% (8,497 votes).

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, Ballotpedia survey or issue-by-issue statements found as of Oct. 19, 2026. A March 2026 Mining Gazette forum report paraphrases her platform as viewing the economic system as insufficient; no quotable statements on guide issues.

candidates.name: Zebulon Featherly

summary.text: Featherly is an independent candidate on the general-election ballot for Michigan's 1st District. A northern Michigan native, he has worked as an electrician and wind turbine technician and describes his campaign as outside the party system.

background.text: Born in Houghton, Michigan; earned a high school diploma from Houghton High School.
Attended Eastern Michigan University and graduated from the North Western Renewable Energy Institute in 2017.
Has worked as an electrician and wind turbine technician; in his Ballotpedia survey he describes himself as an apprentice electrician who was born and raised in northern Michigan.

priorities.text: Strengthening education, health care and clean energy.
priorities.quote: America’s future depends on how well we take care of our people today. By strengthening education, healthcare, and clean energy, we give every American the chance to thrive and keep our nation leading in innovation and opportunity.
Trust in government comes from openness and accountability.

positions.summary: Campaign website supports a government-run single-payer health care system funded through progressive income taxes.
positions.quote: Zebulon supports a government-run single-payer healthcare system

positions.summary: Campaign website supports access to abortion up to 24 weeks of pregnancy, with later procedures requiring medical approval.
positions.quote: Zebulon supports the ability to obtain an abortion up to 24 weeks of pregnancy, with procedures after that time requiring medical approval.

positions.summary: Campaign website supports requiring a background check for every firearm purchase, while also stating support for the Second Amendment.
positions.quote: Everyone purchasing a firearm should be required to complete a background check, regardless of where the purchase occurs.

positions.summary: Campaign website says he does not support blanket tariffs.
positions.quote: Zebulon does not support blanket tariffs.

positions.summary: Campaign website says he does not support using U.S. taxpayer dollars to fund Israel's military.
positions.quote: Zebulon Does not support using American Taxpayer Dollars to fund Israel’s Military

positions.summary: Campaign website supports higher income tax brackets for high incomes and a 5% annual tax on net wealth above $1 billion.
positions.quote: Zebulon supports higher income tax brackets for those with incomes above certain thresholds.

positions.summary: Campaign website supports a nationwide minimum wage increase, starting between $15 and $20 per hour with regional adjustments.
positions.quote: Zebulon supports a country wide minimum wage increase

positions.summary: Campaign website calls reducing reliance on fossil fuels a priority and supports renewable-energy investment, but does not support eliminating fossil fuels entirely at this time.
positions.quote: Zebulon does not support the total elimination of fossil fuels as an energy source at this time.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions come from the Stances page of his campaign website, which is written in the third person and describes itself as a fluid document; priorities come from his 2025 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.

statements.quote: Zebulon supports restructuring federal immigration enforcement by dissolving ICE and redistributing its responsibilities among other agencies.
statements.context: On his campaign website Stances page, written in the third person (page undated; accessed Oct. 19, 2026)

statements.quote: Zebulon supports innovation in housing construction to reduce building costs and increase housing supply.

researchNotes: This is a safe Republican seat (R+11); research time focused on the two major-party candidates. Minor-party and independent candidates have minimal public records beyond their ballot listing. Biographical details beyond the ballot listing were not found for Arnett Satterla or Doc Kovaly; LaVeta Davenport and Liz Hakola have only brief public biographies. Barr's campaign website could not be loaded, so her biography relies on news coverage and Ballotpedia.
